appendix.title: Windows, Linux and macOS
appendix.para: The bridge behaves the same on the three systems; this appendix lists what differs, and the environment variables it reads.

listitem.para: The desktop framework. The bridge's runtime configuration names Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App (Windows Forms, WPF, System.Drawing, system sounds, the event log, SystemEvents) next to Microsoft.NETCore.App. Without the .NET Desktop Runtime everything works but those types (). When .NET already runs without the desktop framework (a .NET application that hosts ooRexx), the bridge uses its other configuration, Rexx.Net.core.runtimeconfig.json.

STA threads. Every Rexx thread becomes a single-threaded apartment at its first request to .NET, as .NET's user interface applications ([STAThread]) and PowerShell's threads are: common dialogs, the clipboard, drag and drop and COM events need it. A thread whose COM is already initialized is left alone, and so are a .NET host's own threads. REXXNET_APARTMENT=MTA leaves every thread alone.

Assemblies by name, locally. .net~load(name) looks for name.dll in the current directory, then next to the bridge, when the runtime does not know the name: an assembly that was in .NET Framework's global cache and is a NuGet package today (System.Speech) is found by copying its .dll there (the binary release carries System.Speech.dll).
COM objects and their events exist on Windows only ().

The installer. Each release has oorexxnet-version-setup.exe, which installs the bridge into an installed ooRexx, with Start menu shortcuts (these books among them) and an uninstaller in Settings > Apps. It is not signed: Windows may say "Windows protected your PC" (More info, then Run anyway), as for ooRexx's own installer.

The native library is librexxnet.so (Linux) or librexxnet.dylib (macOS). Installed, it is in ooRexx's lib, and nothing needs setting. Used from a build directory, the directory goes on the library path (LD_LIBRARY_PATH, DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH) and on REXX_PATH. macOS drops DYLD_* variables when it starts /bin/sh, which ADDRESS SYSTEM uses: give them in the command itself.
.NET in your home. A .NET installed into ~/.dotnet (Microsoft's dotnet-install script) is found through DOTNET_ROOT.

Calls into ooRexx on the main thread. On Linux, ooRexx before 5.3.0 r13267 makes every call into the interpreter from a process's main thread slow (about 200 µs) in a process with many memory mappings, as a .NET one has (ooRexx bug #2106). A .NET application that calls Rexx often needs r13267 or later.
The .NET installation to start, when it is not the system's.
For a .NET application: the directory where rexxnet (and, in guest mode, net.cls) are looked for, after the application's own ().
Windows: MTA keeps the bridge from making Rexx threads single-threaded apartments.
ooRexx's own: where net.cls is found when the bridge is not installed.
